options.content:
Streamlit + BLIP image captioning running on CPU. Read it top to bottom: is it up, how busy and how fast is it, who is using it, what it costs the app, what it costs the laptop, and finally app vs laptop side by side.  
Colours are colour-blind safe (blue = single, orange = bulk) and lines also differ by style (solid / dashed / dotted). Hover the (i) on a panel to see what it shows. Refreshes every 5s.

panels.title: App status
panels.description: up{job="caption_app"}: 1 if Prometheus could scrape the app, 0 if not.

panels.title: node_exporter status
panels.description: up{job="node"}: whether laptop metrics are coming in.

panels.title: Model loaded
panels.description: caption_model_loaded: 1 after BLIP is loaded.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the app started. Drops to 0 if it restarts.

panels.title: Images captioned
panels.description: Total successful captions since the app started.

panels.title: Alerts firing
panels.description: Alerts from rules.yml that are firing right now. 0 means all good.

panels.title: Throughput - images captioned per second
panels.description: How many images get captioned per second (30s window), split by single and bulk uploads.

panels.title: Latency - model time per image (p50, p95, p99)
panels.description: Percentiles from the caption_inference_seconds histogram over 1 min. If p99 moves away from p50, some images are much slower.

panels.title: Time per upload - average, single vs bulk
panels.description: From the caption_request_seconds summary: _sum / _count. A bulk upload is a whole zip, so it is much bigger than single (hence log scale).

panels.title: Error rate - last 5 min
panels.description: Failed images / all images in the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Errors by type - since app start
panels.description: caption_errors_total split by the exception name.

panels.title: Uploads by client IP - since app start
panels.description: caption_requests_total grouped by client_ip ('localhost' when used locally).

panels.title: Uploads by session - since app start
panels.description: caption_requests_total grouped by Streamlit session id and mode.

panels.title: Work in progress - active requests and bulk queue
panels.description: caption_active_requests = uploads being processed now. caption_bulk_queue = images still waiting inside zips.

panels.title: App memory - RAM used by the app
panels.description: caption_memory_bytes (RSS). The model alone is around 1GB, so a flat line around there is normal.

panels.title: App CPU - CPU used by the app
panels.description: caption_cpu_percent. 100% = one full core; PyTorch uses several cores so it can go above 100%.

panels.title: CPU - busy % (user and system)
panels.description: From node_cpu_seconds_total, averaged over all cores. user = mostly PyTorch doing the maths.

custom.axisLabel: CPU busy (% of all cores, linear)

panels.title: RAM - % in use
panels.description: macOS: (wired + active + compressed) / total. Linux: 1 - available / total. The query handles both.

targets.expr: 100 * ((1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes) or ((node_memory_wired_bytes + node_memory_active_bytes + node_memory_compressed_bytes) / node_memory_total_bytes))

panels.title: Disk - free space on /
panels.description: node_filesystem_avail_bytes / node_filesystem_size_bytes for the main disk.

panels.title: Network - bytes in and out per second
panels.description: node_network_*_bytes_total for real interfaces (loopback left out). The big spike at the start is the model download.

panels.title: Laptop CPU vs bulk uploads
panels.description: Blue (left axis): laptop CPU busy %. Orange dashed (right axis): bulk images captioned per second. Purple dotted: images still queued. When a zip is uploaded, both go up together - the CPU spike comes from the bulk job.

panels.title: Laptop RAM vs app memory
panels.description: Blue (left axis): laptop RAM used %. Orange dashed (right axis): the app's own memory. Shows how much of the RAM the model takes.

targets.expr: 100 * ((1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes) or ((node_memory_wired_bytes + node_memory_active_bytes + node_memory_compressed_bytes) / node_memory_total_bytes))
